APP_TUTORIAL_1:
Triple Triad is played by placing cards on a three-by-three grid.
The player to act first is decided at random.
APP_TUTORIAL_2: A variety of rules exist that change how the game is played, but let's start you off with an easy one - All Open! This rule allows you to see all of your opponent's cards.
APP_TUTORIAL_3: I'll go first this time to show you how it's done. I'll also extend the turn limit so you have plenty of time to think!
APP_TUTORIAL_4: Now it's your turn! Place a card in one of the empty spaces adjacent to my card.
APP_TUTORIAL_5: The numbers you can see each correspond to one side of the card. Try choosing a card with a bigger number than mine on the adjacent side!
APP_TUTORIAL_6:
See how my card changed color?
This means you have "captured" the card.
APP_TUTORIAL_7: During your turn, even if you play a card with a smaller number, it will not result in that card being captured.
APP_TUTORIAL_8:
Try to capture and control more cards than your opponent!
The match will end when all spaces on the grid have been filled.
APP_TUTORIAL_9: And the match is over! Whoever controls the most cards at the end of the game is the winner!
APP_LESSONS_ALL_DONE: Every lesson finished, the exam included. Any of them will play again if you want the practice — and the rule book has the five rules the course had no room for.
APP_LESSON_SAME_1: Here is a rule with a name: Same. Two of my cards are still out there — one to the right of the middle square, one below it.
APP_LESSON_SAME_2: Look at the card in your hand. Its right side is a 2, and so is the side it would touch. Its bottom is a 3, and so is the top of the card underneath. Play it in the middle.
APP_LESSON_SAME_DONE: Two sides matched exactly, so both cards turned — and neither of your numbers was the bigger one. That is Same.
APP_LESSON_PLUS_1: Now Plus, and this time nothing of yours is stronger: both of my cards show a 7 where your card shows a 4.
APP_LESSON_PLUS_2: So add each pair instead. Above the middle: 4 and 7, eleven. To its left: 4 and 7, eleven again. Two totals that match is all Plus asks for. Play it in the middle.
APP_LESSON_PLUS_DONE: Both taken by a card weaker than either of them. Plus never asks which number is bigger — only whether the two totals come out the same.
APP_LESSON_COMBO_1: Same once more: your right side against the card beside it, your bottom against the card below. But watch what happens after the two of them turn.
APP_LESSON_COMBO_2: The card you are about to take at the bottom has a 4 on its left, and my last card next to it shows only a 3. The moment it is yours, it turns that one too.
APP_LESSON_COMBO_DONE: Three cards from one placement. Anything captured by Same or Plus attacks its own neighbours in turn, and that chain is the combo — it is not a rule, and it never stops applying.
APP_LESSONS_BLURB: Twelve short lessons, one rule at a time, ending in a real match. Nothing here counts towards your record — play them in any order, as often as you like.
APP_LESSON_SAME_WALL_1: This one uses the edge of the board. Play along the top row and the wall above you counts as a card showing an A.
APP_LESSON_SAME_WALL_2: Your card has an A on top, so the wall matches it. Now you only need one more: its bottom is a 4, and so is the top of my card below. Play it in the empty space up there.
APP_LESSON_SAME_WALL_DONE: The wall counted as the second match, so a single neighbour was enough. That is Same Wall — and it is the one rule you cannot use from the middle of the board.
APP_LESSON_REVERSE_1: Reverse turns the whole game over: the *lower* number wins. Everything you have learned about big numbers is backwards for this one.
APP_LESSON_REVERSE_2: My card above shows a 7. Yours shows a 4 on the side that would touch it — and a 4 is lower, so it wins. Play it in the middle.
APP_LESSON_REVERSE_DONE: Your 4 took my 7. Under Reverse a hand full of small numbers is a strong hand, and an A is nearly worthless.
APP_LESSON_FALLEN_ACE_1: Fallen Ace is one rule about one number: an A stops being a 10 and becomes worth nothing at all.
APP_LESSON_FALLEN_ACE_2: My card above shows an A on the side facing you. Yours shows a 1 — and against a fallen ace, a 1 is enough. Play it in the middle.
APP_LESSON_FALLEN_ACE_DONE: A 1 took an A. Only the ace falls: every other number on my card is worth exactly what it says.
APP_LESSON_REVERSE_FALLEN_ACE_1: Now both together, and they do something neither does alone. Under Reverse your A is the worst side you own; Fallen Ace makes it worth nothing.
APP_LESSON_REVERSE_FALLEN_ACE_2: Nothing is lower than nothing — so the A is unbeatable again. Play the card in the middle and take mine below with its bottom A.
APP_LESSON_REVERSE_FALLEN_ACE_DONE: Two rules that each weaken an ace, and together they hand it back the board. Read the rules before a match; the two of them meeting changes which cards you should bring.
APP_LESSON_ELEMENTAL_1: Under Elemental some squares carry an element, and a card standing on one is stronger or weaker for it: one higher if the element is its own, one lower if it is not.
APP_LESSON_ELEMENTAL_2: The middle square is lightning, and so is your card. Its top is a 2 — the same as the card above, which would normally settle nothing — but on that square it fights as a 3. Play it in the middle.
APP_LESSON_ELEMENTAL_DONE: A tie became a capture, and nothing on either card changed: the square did it. Look at the board before you choose a square — under this rule they are not the same as each other.
APP_LESSON_BONUS_1: Bonus counts tribes. Every card in your hand belongs to the beast tribe — that is the little icon in the corner of each one — and not a single card of mine belongs to any tribe at all.
APP_LESSON_BONUS_2: Every beast that goes down makes all the beasts on the board stronger, on all four sides at once. Watch for the badge under your cards: it says what the board is doing to them.
APP_LESSON_BONUS_3: Two of yours are down now, and the badge has grown with them. It will keep growing — the last card you play will be worth more than it was when I dealt it to you, and nothing printed on it will have changed.
APP_LESSON_BONUS_DONE: Malus is the same count with the sign turned round: every card of a tribe makes all of them weaker. Neither rule touches a number you can read off a card — the badge is the only place the count shows.
APP_LESSON_ORDER_1: Order takes the choice out of your hands. You will play your five cards in the order they were dealt, left to right, and only the first of them will let you pick it up.
APP_LESSON_ORDER_2: So the question stops being which card and becomes which square. Look along the rest of your hand before you place this one — you already know exactly what is coming after it.
APP_LESSON_ORDER_3: Two gone, three to come, and no surprises in them. A hand under Order is a queue you can read to the end, which is more than can ever be said for mine.
APP_LESSON_ORDER_DONE: Chaos asks the same of you and tells you less: instead of taking your cards in order it picks one of them at random, every turn. The habit is the same — stop choosing the card, start choosing the square.
APP_LESSON_EXAM_START: No more lessons — this is a real match. Identical, Plus and Inverse, all three at once, and I am playing to win this time. Good luck.
APP_LESSON_EXAM_WIN: Beaten at my own table, and under three rules at once. You did not need me for that one — go and find someone your own size.
APP_LESSON_EXAM_LOSE: My match. Nothing lost by it — go back through any lesson you like, they are all still there, and then come and take this one from me.
APP_LESSON_EXAM_DRAW: A draw, which against three rules at once is no small thing. Play it again — the cards fall differently every time.
